metadata.creator: Sheehan, Murray
metadata.description: Murray Sheehan, superintendent of the Students' Department of the Siamese Legation, writes to Miss Marshall, secretary to the president of Miami University. He provides M. C. Prasobsukh Sukhsavasti's address in Bangkok, Siam, and discusses his occupation, requesting that Miami University not grant him the title "Prince" in its 1938 graduate files. Sheehan notes that Aurella Rosser identified the recipient only as "Miss Marshall."
metadata.title: Letter to Miss Marshall from Murray Sheehan concerning Prasobsukh Sukhsavasti, 27 October 1938

October 27, 1938

Secretary to the President Miami University Oxford, Ohio

My dear Miss Marshall:

Miss Aurella Rosser has written to say that you would like to have Mr. [Mister] Prasobsukh Sukhsavasti's present address and occupation for the 1938 graduate files.

Mr. Sukhsavasti should be listed as M. C. [Mom Chao] Prasobsukh Sukhsavasti, 10 Pra Aditya Road, Bangkok, Siam [Thailand]. I should like again, as on previous occasions, to request that the [underlined: title of] "Prince" be not granted to him by Miami University, [underlined: despite] Mr. Sukhsavasti's own apparent wide publicity on that score.

His position in Siam may be, as before, a high-school teacher, or he may now be granted a position on one of the Government offices.

Unfortunately, Miss Rosser named you only as "Miss Marshall," so I am unable to address you more fully.

Yours very truly,

[handwritten] Murray Sheehan

Superintendent
